clue.text: Caught a musical, say, about Charlie, a real money earner

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: the show goes around the letter for Charlie, enclosing it

parts.note: a musical is one example of a stage show
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone caught a musical that was about a man named Charlie, and it made a fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: A cash cow is an idiom for a product or business that reliably brings in profit.

clue.text: Butterfly with tail flying about open piece of land

indicators.note: the tail, its last letter, flies off the butterfly

parts.note: the comma is a British butterfly with comma-shaped marks
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A butterfly flits about with its tail flying over an open field.
explanation.definitionFit: A common is an area of open public land in a village or town.

clue.text: Maybe a lot of cool tea as flu cure is crackers

definitions.text: Maybe a lot of cool tea

indicators.note: crackers means crazy, so the fodder letters go wild into a new order

explanation.surface: Drinking cooled tea as a cure for flu is mad.
explanation.walkthrough: People once poured hot tea into the saucer to cool it before drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: A saucerful of cool tea is the amount a saucer holds, and the 'Maybe' says it is one kind of quantity.

clue.text: Carbon more efficient and less polluting

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon
a lean organisation is efficient, so leaner means more efficient

explanation.surface: Carbon technology that is more efficient and causes less pollution.
explanation.definitionFit: Something less polluting is a comparative of clean, giving off less dirt.

clue.text: Storage facility a great bed used to be in

definitions.meaning: a building where goods are stored

definitions.text: a great bed used to be in
definitions.meaning: the Great Bed of Ware, a huge Elizabethan bed now in the V&A, once stood in an inn at Ware, a house in Ware

explanation.walkthrough: Ware is a town in Hertfordshire; the Great Bed of Ware is a famous four-poster now in London's Victoria and Albert Museum.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot for goods is a storage building; read as a Ware house it is where the bed was kept.

clue.text: Rolled bran flakes with very little appeal all round

parts.note: V is the little, abbreviated form of very

indicators.note: the appeal's two letters sit around the cereal word

parts.note: IT is old slang for sex appeal
bran is the flaky husk of cereal grain, so its flakes are bran

explanation.surface: Rolled oats and bran flakes with very little appeal: a dull breakfast bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: The editor later said a late edit spoilt this clue: it should have said husks, not bran flakes, which is why 'flakes' looks like an anagram signal with nothing to scramble.
explanation.definitionFit: In phonetics a trilled consonant, like a rolled Scottish R, is described as vibrant.

clue.text: Asp that is without power to puncture old queen?

indicators.note: the inner group pierces the queen's letters, sitting inside them

parts.note: VR is Victoria Regina, the old queen Victoria

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the that-is letters surround the power letter

parts.note: IE is the abbreviation of id est, that is
P is the symbol for power

explanation.surface: An asp, with no power, is pressed to bite an old queen, like Cleopatra.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark nods to Cleopatra, killed by an asp; the queen here is Victoria.
explanation.definitionFit: An asp is a type of venomous snake, a species of the snake family.

clue.text: Where there are pins keeping back the galley with key rope

indicators.note: the galley word is kept back, withheld from the pins place

parts.note: pins stand at the end of a bowling alley
taken as written, the last six letters of the pins place
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: A ship's galley kept back from the pins, with a key rope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the galley' reads as a ship's kitchen; it is the letters G-ALLEY taken from BOWLING ALLEY.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowline is a rope from a sail's edge to the bow, and also a knot tied in rope.

clue.text: Note men on Territorial Army vessel

indicators.note: in a down answer the note and men sit on top of the army letters

parts.note: A is a musical note
OR, other ranks, are the ordinary soldiers in the British Army
TA is the abbreviation for the British reserve force

explanation.surface: A notice to soldiers aboard a Territorial Army ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship; it is a blood vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The aorta is the body's main artery, a blood vessel from the heart.

clue.text: Result of crossing Scottish bridge railway keeps ending in Dundee

parts.note: the Tay is Scotland's longest river, flowing past Dundee

indicators.note: the bridge and railway letters keep the ending inside them

parts.note: BR is an abbreviation for bridge

indicators.note: the last letter of the city name is taken

explanation.surface: Crossing the Tay rail bridge into Dundee.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tay Bridge carries the railway into Dundee, so 'crossing' looks like travel; it means a hybrid of two plants.
explanation.definitionFit: The tayberry is a hybrid fruit bred from a blackberry and a raspberry, so the product of plant crossing.

clue.text: Map routes all round Cheddar?

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are turned all round into a new order

explanation.surface: Planning road routes all around the Somerset village of Cheddar.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheddar looks like the Somerset place, a natural fit with map routes; the question mark says it is the cheese. MOUSETRAP is also British slang for cheap, plain cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheddar is an example of the cheese baited in a trap for mice, and the word is slang for ordinary cheese.

clue.text: Argument over railway concern

indicators.note: over in a down-or-across sense signals the argument word turned over, read backwards

parts.note: a row is a noisy argument

explanation.surface: A dispute about the railway causes public concern.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down-or-across sense 'over' reads as reversal; here it turns the argument word round.
explanation.definitionFit: Concern and worry are synonyms, both meaning anxiety.

clue.text: Duck is able to get across eastern sea

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, written O

indicators.note: the able-to word spans across the eastern letter, holding it inside

parts.note: can means is able to

explanation.surface: A duck that can fly across an eastern sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Ocean is a near-synonym for sea, a vast body of salt water.

clue.text: Museum investing millions in cultural inheritance

indicators.note: to invest is to clothe or surround, so the inheritance word wraps around the millions letter

parts.note: heritage is a culture's inheritance from the past
M is the abbreviation for million(s)

explanation.surface: A museum puts millions into preserving cultural heritage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'investing' looks financial beside 'millions' but means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: The State Hermitage in St Petersburg is one of the world's great art museums.

clue.text: One predicting bank clerk's after a lot of money

indicators.note: the clerk comes after the money word in the answer

parts.note: a fortune is a large sum of money
a teller is a clerk at a bank counter

explanation.surface: A bank clerk is chasing a large sum of money.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortune-teller is someone who claims to foresee a person's future.

clue.text: Alpine ewes slide all over the place

indicators.note: the letters are scattered everywhere, into a new order

explanation.surface: Sheep slipping all over a mountainside.
explanation.definitionFit: Edelweiss is a white-flowered plant of the Alps, so an alpine in the gardener's sense.

clue.text: Farcical game's cut short and one croupier's losing support

indicators.note: the game loses its last letter

parts.note: ludo is a board game played with dice and counters
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the croupier word loses the support word from inside

parts.note: taken with its s
a pier is a supporting pillar

explanation.surface: A casino game cut short, a croupier losing support: farcical.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludicrous and farcical are synonyms, meaning absurd enough to laugh at.

clue.text: Bird around with cherries half gone? Who could want that?

indicators.note: the bird surrounds the with letter

parts.note: a tit is a small bird

indicators.note: half the fruit word is gone, leaving its first half

explanation.surface: A bird circling a half-eaten bowl of cherries: who would want it?
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points back at the bird in the surface: a keen birdwatcher would want to see it.
explanation.definitionFit: A twitcher is an obsessive birdwatcher, someone who would be keen to spot that bird.

clue.text: Spring kept looking good

parts.note: a well is a spring of water
preserved means kept or saved

explanation.surface: A spring that has been kept in good condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone well-preserved looks good for their age, an idiom for wearing the years lightly.

clue.text: Historical river meadow

parts.note: past means bygone, historical
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: An old river meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasture is grassland for grazing animals, much like a meadow.

clue.text: Name of famous artist included in opening

indicators.note: the included letters go in the opening

parts.note: a vent is an opening for air
INC is the abbreviation for included or inclusive

explanation.surface: A famous artist's name is included in an exhibition opening.
explanation.definitionFit: Vincent van Gogh is the painter usually known by his first name.

clue.text: Jack skinned salmon in manoeuvre

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in cards

indicators.note: the salmon is skinned, its outer letters removed

parts.note: sockeye is a Pacific salmon

explanation.surface: Jack skinned a salmon while manoeuvring.
explanation.definitionFit: To jockey is to manoeuvre for advantage, as in jockeying for position.

clue.text: Small mammal, disturbed, Welshman's hidden?

indicators.note: the Welshman is hidden inside the disturbed word

parts.note: threw can mean disconcerted, as in 'the question threw me'
Rees is a common Welsh name

explanation.surface: A small creature is upset because a Welshman is hiding from it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' looks like an anagram signal, but it is a synonym meaning thrown off balance.
explanation.definitionFit: Tree shrews are small squirrel-like mammals of South-east Asian forests.

clue.text: Anger arising about Heath, say

indicators.note: in a down answer arising means reading upwards, backwards

parts.note: ire is anger
CA, circa, means about

explanation.surface: Anger growing about Edward Heath, the former British prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: Heath looks like the politician; it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is the botanical genus of heaths and heathers, so heath is an example of it.

clue.text: Hard to tamper with identity

parts.note: to rig is to tamper with fraudulently
ID is short for identity

explanation.surface: It is hard to tamper with someone's identity.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigid means stiff or hard, unable to bend.

clue.text: North American food, mostly

indicators.note: most of the food word is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: chow is slang for food

explanation.surface: A snack from the Americas that is mostly food.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines the answer: a Tex-Mex snack is largely North American food.
explanation.definitionFit: A tortilla chip snack with cheese is a typically North American dish of Mexican origin.

clue.text: What's in Thai, like our Eastern verse

indicators.note: what is inside each of the three words, their ends dropped, is taken

explanation.surface: Asking what poetry from Thailand is like compared with ours.
explanation.walkthrough: The insides of THAI, LIKE and OUR are HA, IK and U.
explanation.definitionFit: A haiku is a short three-line Japanese poem, so Eastern verse.

clue.text: Travellers' aid in electronic Scottish Bible?

indicators.note: the electronic letter goes in the Scots name for the Bible

parts.note: the Bible is the Good Book, and guid is Scots for good
E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-book

explanation.surface: An electronic version of a Scottish Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: A guidebook informs tourists about a place, so it helps people on their travels.

clue.text: Tear on freeway regularly and hit the vehicle in front

indicators.note: the tear word is placed on, after, the picked letters
every other letter of the motorway word is picked, at regular intervals

parts.note: to rend is to tear apart

explanation.surface: Racing along a freeway and running into the car ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: Every other letter of fReEwAy gives REA.
explanation.definitionFit: To rear-end is to crash into the back of another vehicle, so to hit the one ahead.

clue.text: Meet is outside of Filey on Saturday

indicators.note: the pieces follow one another, the day first
the outside letters of the town's name are taken

explanation.surface: A sports meeting is held outside Filey on Saturday.
explanation.walkthrough: Filey is a seaside town in Yorkshire; its outer letters are F and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: To meet a need or demand is to satisfy it, a synonym in that sense.
